question: What primary ion is required for actin and myosin filaments to slide during muscle contraction?
explanation: Calcium ions bind to regulatory proteins on the actin filament, exposing binding sites so myosin can attach and generate contraction. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h1)

question: An intact neuromuscular pathway is necessary for skeletal muscle to achieve which outcome?
explanation: Motor neurons deliver electrical signals from the central nervous system to trigger coordinated muscle fiber contractions. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h1)

question: The primary cause of muscle atrophy during prolonged bed rest is...

options.A: Rapid multiplication of red blood cells
options.C: Decreased protein synthesis and increased breakdown
options.D: Excessive calcium deposition in muscle tissue

explanation: Disuse reduces the metabolic demand for muscle proteins, shifting the cellular balance toward degradation rather than building. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h2)

question: A contracture develops in an immobile joint primarily because of what physiological change?

options.A: Complete destruction of the adjacent bone cortex
options.B: Replacement of muscle fibers with connective tissue
options.C: Massive accumulation of fluid inside the joint capsule
options.D: Sudden elongation of the tendon sheath

explanation: Fibrous connective tissue and collagen shorten around the unused joint, permanently restricting normal movement. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h2)

question: A patient who can move a joint against gravity alone but cannot overcome any resistance has a muscle strength grade of...
explanation: Grade 3 denotes the ability to move the limb against the downward pull of gravity without any added resistance from the examiner. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h3)

question: What does a nurse eliminate when testing a patient with a muscle strength grade of two?

options.A: The effect of gravity on the limb
options.B: All nerve impulses from the spinal cord
options.D: The friction of the bed sheet

explanation: Placing the limb in a horizontal plane removes gravity, allowing weak muscles to show visible movement. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h3)

question: During passive range of motion exercises, the nurse should support the limb in what manner?

options.C: Only at the proximal insertion point

explanation: Supporting both sides of the joint protects vulnerable ligaments and ensures smooth, controlled movement. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why must a nurse stop passive range of motion exercises when meeting sudden firm resistance?

options.A: To test the patient for nerve damage
options.B: To allow the muscle time to produce calcium
options.C: To prevent injury to joint structures

explanation: Forcing a joint past its current barrier of resistance can tear muscle fibers, tendons, and joint capsules. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h4)

question: The primary dietary component required for muscle protein synthesis and repair is...
explanation: Proteins break down into amino acids, which serve as the essential building blocks for repairing and maintaining muscle mass. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is nutritional support critical for a patient experiencing prolonged muscular immobility?

options.A: It stops all electrical activity in the peripheral nerves
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for physical therapy
options.C: It reverses bone fractures within twenty-four hours
options.D: It counters the natural catabolic breakdown of muscle tissue

explanation: Inactivity shifts the body into a catabolic state, making sufficient nutrient intake necessary to slow muscle wasting. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h5)

question: What nursing intervention helps prevent foot drop in a bedridden patient?

options.A: Applying warm compresses to the toes
options.B: Elevating the head of the bed high

explanation: A footboard keeps the feet in a neutral dorsiflexed position, preventing shortening of the Achilles tendon. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h6)

question: How often should a bedridden patient be repositioned to prevent skin breakdown and muscle strain?
explanation: Regular turning every two hours relieves sustained pressure on bony prominences and maintains circulation to compressed tissues. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h6)
